sections.heading: Section 1: Finding Domains of Rational and Radical Functions

questions.answer: Denominator cannot be zero: $x^2 - 16 \neq 0 \Rightarrow x \neq \pm 4$. Domain: all reals except $x = -4$ and $x = 4$.
The radicand must be non-negative: $2x - 8 \geq 0 \Rightarrow 2x \geq 8 \Rightarrow x \geq 4$, which is $[4, \infty)$.
Radicand in denominator must be strictly positive: $9 - x^2 > 0 \Rightarrow x^2 < 9 \Rightarrow -3 < x < 3$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Finding Ranges of Algebraic Functions

questions.answer: Complete the square: $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 + 3$. Since $(x - 2)^2 \geq 0$, the minimum value is 3. Range: $[3, \infty)$.
Domain is $[-5, 5]$. Min occurs at $x = \pm 5$ ($h = 0$). Max occurs at $x = 0$ ($h = 5$). Range is $[0, 5]$.

questions.q: Evaluate $f(-2)$ for $f(x)$ defined as $2x + 1$ for $x < 0$, and $x^2 - 3$ for $x \geq 0$.
Find the domain of $f(x)$ defined as $\frac{1}{x+3}$ for $x < 1$, and $\sqrt{x - 1}$ for $x \geq 1$.
questions.answer: For $x < 1$, $x+3 \neq 0 \Rightarrow x \neq -3$. For $x \geq 1$, $x - 1 \geq 0$ is always true. Domain is all reals except $x = -3$.

questions.q: Determine the range of $g(x)$ defined as $-x$ for $x < 0$, and $x + 1$ for $x \geq 0$.
questions.answer: For $x < 0$, $-x > 0$, giving outputs $(0, \infty)$. For $x \geq 0$, $x + 1 \geq 1$, giving $[1, \infty)$. Union is $(0, \infty)$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Domain and Range of Compositions

questions.q: If $f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 2}$ and $g(x) = \sqrt{x}$, find the domain of $(f \circ g)(x)$.
questions.answer: First, $g(x)$ requires $x \geq 0$. Second, $f(g(x)) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x} - 2}$ requires $\sqrt{x} \neq 2 \Rightarrow x \neq 4$. Domain: $[0, 4) \cup (4, \infty)$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = 3x - 1$, what is the range of $(f \circ g)(x)$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$?
questions.answer: $(f \circ g)(x) = (3x - 1)^2$. Any real squared is non-negative, so the range is $[0, \infty)$.

questions.q: Find the domain of $(g \circ f)(x)$ if $f(x) = 2x + 6$ and $g(x) = \ln(x)$.
questions.answer: $(g \circ f)(x) = \ln(2x + 6)$. The argument of logarithm must be strictly positive: $2x + 6 > 0 \Rightarrow 2x > -6 \Rightarrow x > -3$.
